angle:
Structure level: change which project hosts a case and how a case splits, never what a case reads. Parallelism exists only across the four projects: each project runs one file in series, and its cases share the `proven`, `placed`, and `rows` sets (integration.test.ts:165-168). The wall is therefore the longest project span. In the 761.76 s run, the wall exceeds the four-way mean of summed test time by 203.89 s (2231.49 s / 4 = 557.87 s, journey-5b.log:201). Light-1280 alone carries preservation, partition, and 305.23 s of component tables (journey-4.json:1).

Load-bearing finding: every journey project opens the same Playwright page. The provider options carry only launch options (configs/browsers.ts:289-315), and the provider leaves the context viewport unset outside UI mode (node_modules/@vitest/browser-playwright/dist/index.js:1080-1105). The `buildJourney` helper sets the iframe viewport and applies the theme from the variant object it receives (tests/setupBrowser.ts:1153-1162). A case that passes a fixed variant object therefore reads the same page in any project. Two places in the file already rely on this: preservation and partition read 390x800 inside the light-1280 project (integration.test.ts:1131, 1447), and the frozen refusal reads the other width inside its own project (integration.test.ts:834). Each matrix half can therefore move to another project, and its reading stays the same.

Rulings on the five examples:
(1) Split the two widths across variants: take it (C3, C4), with the reading pinned to the light-1280 variant object.
(2) Share one page build across cases: refuse it (R2).
(3) Move width-invariant proofs to one variant: refuse it (R1).
(4) Run the paired engine case per family across variants: the premise does not hold. Each family already runs one time, in its table's variant (integration.test.ts:864). A per-family split with the reading variant fixed stays as an optional balancing unit (C5).
(5) Merge cases that rebuild the same state: refuse it at the case level (R3). Take it at the attribution level, where three full attributions and three full partitions per width rebuild identical selector matches (C1, C2).

The plan runs one browser measurement at a time on the host, because one full run already loads all 4 CPUs. Two lanes can write the code in parallel.

changes.change: C1. Share the selector matches across the preservation case's three full attributions per width. Give the `collectComponentPreservation` function an optional memo of matched rules per signature element, keyed by `CSSStyleSheet` identity. The preservation case creates one memo per width and passes it to the main attribution and the two reader-control attributions. The three sheet-rewrite controls pass no memo. Hoist each sheet's `selectorText` strings one time per call, because the getter serializes the selector on every read.
changes.files: tests/setupBrowser.ts `collectComponentPreservation` function (1938-2056: the `entries` scan at 1974-1977 and the per-signature `rules` filter at 1990-1995) and its TSDoc remarks; tests/app/browser/integration.test.ts preservation calls at 1215, 1273, and 1282; tests/setupBrowser.test.ts, beside the collector proofs at 1107-1291
changes.basis:
The model saving is 45 s of summed time. All of it falls on light-1280's critical path before C4, and about 11 s of wall after C4.

The T3 reader controls added 66.64 s for four full attributions: 71.17 s of controls in the 761.76 s run (journey-5b.log:97, 127, 139) against 4.53 s before T3 (journey-4.log:65, 89, 97). One full attribution therefore costs 16.66 s under full load. Every attribution re-filters every rule of the served and lifted sheets against each of the 1,458 signatures (journey-5b.log:97). By opening-brace count, the recipe string in app/browser/recipe.json holds 3,133 rules and dist/src/tailwindcss/index.css holds 4,023. That is about 10.4 million `selectorText` reads and `element.matches` calls per attribution. The rest of an attribution visits only changed longhands and the rules that matched.

Sharing removes two of the three filters per width, four filters per run. The 45 s figure assumes the filter is about two thirds of an attribution (four filters x 16.66 s x 0.67). No run separates matching time from the rest of an attribution, so credit only the figure that measurement step 2 reads.
changes.coverage_kept_how:
Every reading and control keeps its inputs:
- The main, wrapping-control, and overflow-control attributions still run with their own `inherited` and `coupled` options and assert what they assert in the T3 tree (integration.test.ts:1215-1300).
- The stripped-curation, preserved-curation, and planted-preflight controls (1314-1426) still match fresh against the rewritten served sheet. A rewritten `style` element owns a different `CSSStyleSheet` object, which a memo keyed by sheet identity never matches.
- New setup proofs pin equal results with and without the memo over the existing fixtures, and show that a memo is not read for a foreign sheet: a planted preflight rule in a second sheet still attributes `preflight`.
- The coupling mutation target `longhand.startsWith('overflow-')` (setupBrowser.ts:2003) stays byte-identical, so the coupling control in tmp/units/tokens-t3/mutations-6.ts still applies.
changes.risk: A memo that outlives a sheet change hides a departure. Three things limit this: the identity key, the foreign-sheet setup proof, and passing the memo only to the three calls that read unmodified sheets. Memory: one matched-rule array per signature element per width, which the case drops at the end of the width.

changes.change: C2. Share the selector matches across the partition case's three full partitions per width. Give the `collectPartition` function an optional memo of each subject's `matched` declarations, keyed by subject element and by the identity of the `options.rules` map. The partition case passes one memo per width to the main, unmapped, and inverse partitions. The subset partitions under adopted control sheets match fresh.
changes.files: tests/setupBrowser.ts `collectPartition` function (2140-2196, the per-subject `matched` build at 2158-2196); tests/app/browser/integration.test.ts partition calls at 1549, 1553, and 1633; tests/setupBrowser.test.ts
changes.basis:
The 20 s figure is a model. The target credits 0 s for C2.

Each full partition filters about 7,589 rules against each of the 1,670 signature elements (journey-5b.log:149, 175). By opening-brace count, those rules are 4,164 in dist/src/bootstrap/index.css, 292 in the unexcluded string, and 3,133 in the recipe string. That is about 12.7 million `element.matches` calls per partition. The main, unmapped, and inverse partitions read the same elements against the same `options.rules` map, so their `matched` maps are identical. The inverse partition replaces only the tailwindcss values, and `resolvePartitionProperty` reads only `values.bootstrap`.

The case reads 84.29 s for both widths in the full run (journey-5b.log:195) and 61.82 s alone (tmp/units/tokens-t3/partition-3-dev.log:46). No run separates matching time from the rest of the case.
changes.coverage_kept_how:
Every partition and control keeps its inputs:

changes.risk: The memo can serve stale declarations, as in C1. The identity keys and a setup proof that compares memo and no-memo results limit this. If measurement shows that matching is a small share of a partition, drop C2: it gains nothing on the wall after C4 unless the partition half sits on the long pole.

changes.change: C3. Split preservation and partition into one case per width, four cases in all. Each half passes the light-1280 variant object with the width it reads (`{ ...LIGHT_1280, width }`), as the loop passes it in the T3 tree. Register each half through an `it.each` over a `JOURNEY_PLACEMENTS` entry of `{ width, host }` pairs filtered to `VARIANT`, as J7 and the refusals register (integration.test.ts:459, 686), so no skip marker appears. Retitle each half from 'at both widths' to 'at WIDTH px', where WIDTH is 1280 or 390. Prefix each preservation and partition row with the reading variant and width, because the row lands in the host project's file. Restore the host viewport in each half's `finally` block, as the case does at 1435 and 1691.

changes.basis:
C3 saves no summed time; it makes C4 possible.

Each case loops `for (const width of [1280, 390])` (integration.test.ts:1129, 1446) with one build per width (1131, 1447). The only state that crosses widths is the preservation case's `failures` list, which it asserts one time at the end (1428). In the 761.76 s run, preservation reads its main scans at 31.26 s and 33.00 s and its controls at 71.17 s (journey-5b.log:97, 127, 139). Partition reads 84.29 s over two widths with equal populations of 8,271 elements and 1,670 signatures (journey-5b.log:149, 175, 195).
changes.coverage_kept_how:
Every assertion, control, log line, and row runs per width as it runs in the loop:
- Each half asserts its own `failures` list.
- The reading keeps the light theme at WIDTHx800, because the `buildJourney` helper applies the viewport and theme from the variant object (setupBrowser.ts:1153-1162). The project's configured viewport does not enter the reading.
- The 390 half starts from the `afterEach` reset (integration.test.ts:195-202) where the loop started from the 1280 half's restored sheets. The `afterEach` reset leaves fewer residues.
- Neither case adds to `proven`, so the portfolio check at 1884 is unaffected.
changes.risk:
Ruling text. The comments at 1122 and 1440 and guides/veneer.md:1966 say the ruling selects light-1280. The reading stays light-1280's, and the host becomes a scheduling choice. The Orchestrator confirms that reading of the rulings before landing.

Count changes. Registered cases change from 96 to 92 and skips from 6 to 0 (journey-5b.log:199), so every run report and the lanes log must use those counts. Scripts under tmp/units that read light-1280.txt for these rows must read the host files.

changes.basis:
C4 saves 133 s of wall (model) and no summed time.

In the 591.13 s run, light-1280 ends at 591.12 s, and dark-1280, light-390, and dark-390 end at 476.86, 465.02, and 396.97 s (journey-4.json:1 `endTime`). The model scales every case the T3 run does not time by 1.16. That factor is 1,715.42 s of untimed T3 time over 1,479.03 s of the same cases in the 591.13 s run (journey-5b.log:201, journey-4.log:169, less the logged bodies). The model uses the logged bodies for J4, paired, preservation, and partition, and sets light-1280's span from the observed wall (761.76 s less a 10.29 s start offset).

Spans after C1: light-1280 706.5 s, dark-1280 530.4 s, light-390 514.0 s, and dark-390 435.6 s. The halves after C1 are about 44.4 s for preservation 1280, 46.1 s for preservation 390, and 42.2 s for each partition half, and the theme table is 11.8 s (10.30 s in journey-4.json:1, x1.16).

After the moves, the spans are 573.9, 530.4, 546.6, and 535.6 s. With the start offsets of 10.29, 15.54, 16.26, and 16.53 s (journey-4.json:1 `startTime`), the projects end at about 584, 546, 563, and 552 s. The wall falls from about 717 s after C1 to about 584 s.
changes.coverage_kept_how: No case, assertion, control, or reading changes. Only the host project changes. The host-bound titles keep their projects: J8 and the accordion table at light-390, and the tooltip, collapse, and navbar-390 tables at dark-390 (lanes.md:58). changes.risk:
Contention. The balanced tail runs under full load, while the T3 light-1280 tail ran with fewer peers. Full load costs 1.43x on paired (59.90 s alone against 85.83 s in the full run: paired-5.log:19, journey-5b.log:59) and 1.15x to 1.21x on J4 (j4-5-isolated.log:9, journey-5b.log:13-19). Expect up to about 20 s on light-1280 beyond the model.

Memory. Up to three projects can hold preservation or partition surfaces at once; in the T3 tree only light-1280 does. J0c read a peak of 12,288,905,216 bytes against a 14,345,035,776-byte cap with 60 cases (j0c-report.md:117). The T3 peak is unread, so measure it.

Load-sensitive titles. A table that fails only under the changed load profile is a defect, not a host-bound title.

changes.change: C5 (optional). Split the paired engine case into one case per family through an `it.each` over the variant's tables. Each case passes its table's variant object to the `buildJourney` and `buildComponent` helpers and reads that variant's theme for the popover clicks, so a family can run in another project with an unchanged reading. Move one light-1280 family, such as alert, to the project with the most slack. Take C5 only if measurement B0 leaves light-1280 more than one family above the next project.

target_basis:
The target is 590 s, measured in the same way as the 761.76 s T3 final run (journey-5b.log:201), with 92 cases registered and none skipped.

The target counts C1 at 45 s and C3 and C4. C2 is credited at 0 s.
- The per-project model in C4 ends the four projects at about 584, 546, 563, and 552 s.
- The balanced tail of light-1280 runs under full load, at 1.15x to 1.43x a lighter-loaded reading (paired-5.log:19 against journey-5b.log:59; j4-5-isolated.log:9 against journey-5b.log:13-19). That can add up to about 20 s.
- C5 recovers about 16 s when measurement B0 shows that light-1280 is still the long pole.
- The modeled range is 568 to 603 s.

Cross-check by summed time. After C1 the summed time is 2231.49 - 45 = 2186.5 s. Allow up to 30 s more for the tail under full load. Divided by 4, that gives about 554 s. Add the 10 to 17 s start offsets (journey-4.json:1) and about 10 s of residual imbalance from piece granularity: about 580 s.

Run-to-run spread on the same tree is large: 761.76, 872.76, and 895.58 s (journey-5b.log:201, journey-5.log:185, flip-gates-2/test:journey.log:201). The structure change is therefore also judged by a measure that does not depend on host load: wall minus summed test time over 4. That measure reads 203.89 s in the 761.76 s run and must read 30 s or less after the change. If baseline B0's summed test time differs from 2231.49 s, restate the target as (B0 summed - measured C1 and C2 savings + 30) / 4 + 30 s.

The structure gains compose with wait-level and row-level cuts from other angles. Those cuts lower the summed time, and this plan turns that lower sum into wall time.
measurement_plan:
Order and parallelism:
- Run every browser measurement alone on the host, under `flock /home/user/.wave/journey.lock` as J0c did (j0c-brief.md:22, 89). Start after the token units land and the other lane's browser suites end. One full run already loads all 4 CPUs with four Chromium instances (paired: 59.90 s alone, 85.83 s in the full run; paired-5.log:19, journey-5b.log:59), so a concurrent run distorts both readings.
- Parallelize the writing. Lane A writes C1 and C2 with their setup proofs. Lane B writes C3, C4, C5, and the guide edits in a separate worktree. Lane B rebases onto lane A's three changed call sites per case before it measures. A reviewer reads each lane's diff while the other lane measures.

Steps:
1. Baseline B0 on the landed tree. Run one full journey through the J0c sampler: `node tmp/codex/j0b-measure.ts B0 ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config configs/app/vite.journey.config.ts --no-cache --reporter=dot --reporter=json --outputFile=tmp/units/UNIT/journey-b0.json`, where UNIT names the tuning unit's folder (j0c-brief.md:248). Before the run, add a log of per-call seconds for the three full attributions and the three full partitions per width; this adds a reading and removes none. B0 records per-case seconds for all 96 cases, per-project `startTime` and `endTime`, and the memory peak; the T3 runs lack all three.
2. Matching-share probe. Run one scoped preservation run with a timer around setupBrowser.ts:1990-1995. Keep the timer in tmp/units and never commit it. Replace C1's 45 s model with the figure the probe reads.
3. C1 and C2, scoped. Run `--project journey:light-1280 -t TITLE` two times before and two times after, for the preservation title and the partition title. Success requires all of the following:
   - Every reading line equals B0's apart from time fields. The lines are: Component preservation (causes, exclusions, propagated, departures, and lost), Component repaired causes, Component reader controls, the three Component control lines, Partition, the six Partition population lines, Partition unmapped control, Primary map demonstration, Partition role control, and the four Partition control lines per width.
   - `test:setup:browser` passes with the memo proofs.
   - `node tmp/units/tokens-t3/mutations-6.ts` reads each of its four controls red, then green after restore.
   - The case seconds fall.
4. C3 to C5, scoped. Run each split case one time in its destination project and record its seconds (J0c rule: j0c-brief.md:219). Choose the final homes from B0's measured spans: place the largest piece first into the project with the most slack, use the fewest moves, and keep the host-bound titles fixed (lanes.md:58). Take C5 only if the projected long pole still exceeds the next project by more than one family.
5. Acceptance. Run two consecutive full runs with the JSON reporter and the sampler. Each run succeeds when all of the following hold:
   - 92 cases are registered and 0 are skipped (96 and 6 in the T3 tree: journey-5b.log:199).
   - Every failure is a § Host-bound set title (lanes.md:58). A failure outside the set blocks the landing, because a row that fails only under full load is a defect (j0c-scope.md:36).
   - The per-kind reading lines, including the 18 Engine equality rows, equal B0's under a comparison script in tmp/units that ignores time fields. tmp/units/tokens-t3/extract-evidence.ts can produce the sets.
   - The union of rows across the four tmp/journey files equals B0's union, apart from the reading-variant prefix.
   - The wall reads 590 s or less.
   - Wall minus summed test time over 4 reads 30 s or less (203.89 s in the 761.76 s run).
   - The memory peak stays under the 14,345,035,776-byte cap, and the run report records the peak.
   - `check`, `lint:check`, `format:check`, `test:setup:browser`, `test:guides`, and `test:policy` exit 0.
6. Record. Record B0, both acceptance runs, the per-project spans, and the placement chosen in the lanes log. Update the guide's Variant placement table and partition paragraph in the same commit as the placement.
